items.description: Read the full requirements and Appendix A; identify every mandatory section, diagram, and formatting rule; create the team outline.
items.expectedOutput: Report outline and requirements checklist.

items.description: Use only the official comma.ai product overview for advertised features, general purpose, driver responsibility, and product-level limitations; use EECS 4314 materials for architecture concepts; separate product facts from Group H proposals.
items.expectedOutput: Product-level research notes with a clear facts-versus-proposals distinction.

items.description: Write the introduction and overview covering advertised purpose and features, motivation, objectives, scope, report organization, and the statement that Group H is proposing a conceptual design rather than documenting the real implementation.
items.expectedOutput: Approximately 1–1.5 pages of introduction and overview.

items.description: Write a provisional abstract covering purpose, proposed subsystem groups, intended cooperation, architectural qualities, trade-offs to evaluate, and objectives; revise it only after completed teammate sections are available.
items.expectedOutput: Approximately two-thirds of a page, marked provisional until integration.

items.description: Integrate all sections, diagrams, and references; review completeness, terminology, labels, citations, duplication, focus, and page count.
items.expectedOutput: One coherent, reviewed 10–15 page report.

items.description: Create and verify the final PDF, publish it on the Group H site, test its links, and complete submission.
items.expectedOutput: Verified publication link and submitted report.

items.description: Review EECS 4314 architecture concepts, the official comma.ai product overview, and Group H's presentation; establish design goals and agreed vocabulary without examining OpenPilot implementation sources.
items.expectedOutput: Course-based conceptual architecture notes and an assumptions list.

items.description: Define the agreed proposed subsystems, external actors, responsibilities, information inputs and outputs, interactions, dependencies, and course-based reasons for separation.
items.expectedOutput: Proposed subsystem inventory with responsibilities, information inputs and outputs, dependencies, rationale, and assumptions.

items.description: Evaluate modular separation, message-oriented or publish-subscribe communication, a pipeline-like driving path, feedback control, and layered responsibilities as proposed design choices; explain benefits and limitations without claiming actual implementation use.
items.expectedOutput: Course-justified architectural-style proposal.

items.description: Create a labeled overall architecture diagram of the proposed subsystems, external actors, and meaningful relationships; visibly identify it as Group H's proposed conceptual model.
items.expectedOutput: Proposed architecture diagram in SVG or PNG format.

items.description: Create a conceptual dependency diagram with clear directions, a legend, and assumptions; keep dependencies distinct from data flow.
items.expectedOutput: Proposed dependency diagram in SVG or PNG format with legend and assumptions.

items.description: Write the section explaining proposed subsystems, responsibilities, interactions, styles, dependencies, strengths, limitations, and assumptions; cite course concepts and product facts separately.
items.expectedOutput: Referenced 2–3 page conceptual section plus both diagrams.

items.description: Use the agreed Group H model and EECS 4314 concepts to define proposed producers, consumers, and implementation-neutral information categories for observations, interpretations, plans, control requests, vehicle state, attention status, and alerts.
items.expectedOutput: Conceptual flow notes with proposed producers, consumers, information categories, and assumptions.

items.description: Trace a proposed adaptive cruise control scenario through observations, perception results, planning decisions, control requests, the vehicle boundary, and updated vehicle-state feedback using the agreed subsystem names.
items.expectedOutput: Proposed end-to-end ACC data-flow narrative.

items.description: Explain proposed startup readiness, engagement conditions, decision communication, feedback, disengagement, and handling of delayed or unavailable information.
items.expectedOutput: Proposed control-flow analysis with explicit assumptions and rationale.

items.description: Analyze which conceptual responsibilities could operate concurrently, how a proposed Messaging Layer would coordinate information, why timing matters, and how the design should react to delayed or invalid inputs.
items.expectedOutput: Conceptual concurrency proposal and timing assumptions.

items.description: Create sequence diagram 1 for adaptive cruise control responding to a slower vehicle using only proposed subsystem names and conceptual information categories; label the diagram as Group H's proposal.
items.expectedOutput: Proposed ACC sequence diagram in SVG or PNG format.

items.description: Write the section explaining proposed data flow, control flow, concurrency, the sequence diagram, architectural implications, and assumptions.
items.expectedOutput: Referenced 2–3 page conceptual analysis and sequence diagram.

items.description: Use the official comma.ai product overview only for advertised product behaviour, then use Group H's proposed model to identify conceptual boundaries with the Driver, Car, Sensors & Cameras, and User Interface; separate product facts from design assumptions.
items.expectedOutput: Proposed system-boundary inventory with facts and assumptions clearly separated.

items.description: For each proposed external interface, document the external actor, conceptual information entering and leaving, proposed subsystem owner, intended use, and any assumptions.
items.expectedOutput: Proposed external-interface table with explicit assumptions.

items.description: Describe lane centering, adaptive cruise control, and driver monitoring as conceptual use cases with actor, preconditions, trigger, main flow, alternatives, result, and proposed subsystems; connect advertised features to Group H's design without claiming the real implementation works this way.
items.expectedOutput: Three complete conceptual use-case descriptions.

items.description: Create a proposed sequence or state diagram for a distracted-driver scenario using Driver Monitoring, Self-Drive Supervisor, Controls, Vehicle Interface, User Interface, Driver, and Car where relevant; label all interactions as Group H's proposal.
items.expectedOutput: Labeled proposed driver-monitoring sequence or state diagram.

items.description: Write the conceptual external-interfaces and use-cases section, explain the distracted-driver diagram, and clearly distinguish official product facts from Group H proposals and assumptions.
items.expectedOutput: Referenced 2–3 page conceptual section, interface table, use cases, and labeled diagram.

items.description: Review the proposed architecture, flow, and interface work from Spence, Mehdi, and David; identify important design decisions, assumptions, gaps, and terminology conflicts.
items.expectedOutput: Consolidated review notes for Group H's conceptual architecture.

items.description: Analyze the trade-offs of the proposed modular separation, Messaging Layer, pipeline and feedback-control ideas, responsiveness, reliability, maintainability, extensibility, driver and vehicle boundaries, and support for compatible vehicles.
items.expectedOutput: Course-based trade-off analysis with benefits, challenges, assumptions, and implications.

items.description: Explain possible developer responsibility areas suggested by Group H's subsystem boundaries and the coordination needed across proposed interfaces; do not claim these are OpenPilot's real teams or implementation structure.
items.expectedOutput: Conceptual developer-responsibility discussion grounded in the proposed architecture.

items.description: Create a conceptual data dictionary for Road Observation, Driver Observation, Vehicle State, Perception Result, Desired Path, Target Speed, Control Request, Attention Status, Alert, and Engagement State, using the columns Term, Type or Category, Conceptual Meaning, and Proposed Producers or Consumers.
items.expectedOutput: Implementation-neutral conceptual data dictionary.

items.description: Document Group H's subsystem and information-category naming conventions so every section and diagram uses the agreed terms consistently; do not present these names as actual OpenPilot implementation names.
items.expectedOutput: Concise Group H naming-convention guide.

items.description: Propose architecture-level validation and reliability checks covering responsibility coverage, interface contracts, feedback, stale or missing information, inconsistent state, driver alerts, bounded control requests, and scenario walkthroughs using course concepts rather than implementation sources.
items.expectedOutput: Short conceptual validation-and-reliability plan.

items.description: Write lessons learned and conclusions about the strengths, limitations, unresolved assumptions, improvements, and future directions of Group H's proposed architecture; do not draw conclusions about the real implementation.
items.expectedOutput: Lessons-learned and conclusions section for the proposal.

items.description: Collect, deduplicate, verify, and consistently format references from every member; reject unsupported product claims, implementation sources, and architecture claims that are not labeled as Group H proposals or assumptions.
items.expectedOutput: Consolidated reference list and evidence-boundary check.
